subject: Operations
title: Vertical Integration
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Vertical Integration.

hook.text: A steel company buys iron mines and car factories. It now controls the entire chain from ore to automobile.

buildup.text: Vertical integration means owning multiple stages of the supply chain—upstream, downstream, or both.

discovery.text: It provides control over quality, supply, and margins. But it also locks capital into fixed assets.

twist.text: Highly integrated firms struggle to adapt when markets shift—every owned stage must be retooled, not just renegotiated.

climax.text: Netflix vertically integrated from distribution into content production—owning the show and the screen.

punchline.text: Own the chain for control. Outsource for agility.

quiz.question: What is a downside of vertical integration?
options: Reduced flexibility to adapt to market changes
